sources_fetched.title: Asana Developers - API, Documentation & Community Support • Asana

record.name: Asana
record.one_liner: Asana's public developer platform provides a REST API, webhooks, and app components, using OAuth 2.0 or personal access tokens for authentication.

auth.notes: Asana supports OAuth 2.0 as the preferred method for applications to access the API on behalf of a user, and also supports personal access tokens (PATs) and Service Accounts.

access.notes: Developers can create a free account, test workspaces, request developer sandboxes, and create apps or personal access tokens directly via the developer console.

api_surface.notes: The Asana API is a RESTful interface, and the platform also features webhooks and app components.

mcp.notes: Reported value was discarded: no support offered.

buildability.reasoning: Credentials are self-serve (oauth2) and the pages document a usable API surface. (Derived from access, auth and api_surface.)

evidence.quote: At its core, OAuth ("Open Authorization") is a mechanism for applications to access the Asana API on behalf of a user, all without the application having access to the user's username and password.

evidence.claim: Developers can self-serve credentials and test workspaces
evidence.quote: Choose your test workspace. You can test in any of your existing workspaces, create a free account, or request a developer sandbox.
The Asana API is a RESTful interface with predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts JSON or form-encoded requests, returns JSON, and uses standard HTTP features (verbs, response codes, etc.)
Automate tedious work in powerful, bespoke ways with our platform          features like rule actions, webhooks, and our API.
